title: 268. Permutation Sequence

examples.explanation: Among the 24 orderings of 1..4, the 9th in sorted order is 2314.
The first ordering is the digits in increasing order.

hints: There are (n-1)! orderings starting with each choice for the first digit, so divide (k-1) by (n-1)! to pick it.
Convert k to 0-based, then repeatedly select index k / fact and update k = k % fact with shrinking factorials.
Keep the remaining digits in a list and remove the chosen digit at each step.
